subject.title: [bug]：Gateway pairing failure on Trim OS / TerraMaster NAS: WebSocket closes with code 1002 during device proof response

question: Should this Trim OS packaged Gateway failure be handled as a core Gateway auth/protocol repair, an external package/config-management follow-up, or kept blocked until redacted connect-frame and Gateway-log proof identifies the failing path?
rationale: The reported workaround and possible fixes touch Gateway device pairing, shared auth, and a package manager that may live outside this repository, so automation should not choose an auth-bypass or config-policy change from source inspection alone.

options.title: Collect proof before auth changes
options.body: Ask for redacted Gateway logs, the failed `connect` frame details, exact CLI/Gateway/package versions, and before/after generated config before changing code or packaging.

options.title: Core diagnostic repair
options.body: If logs prove a current OpenClaw client speaks the wrong protocol or diagnostics are opaque, fix Gateway/CLI diagnostics without loosening pairing or shared auth.

options.title: Route package-owned config rewrite
options.body: If only `trim.openclaw` regenerates `gateway.auth` outside this tree, keep core secure and route the config-management change to that package owner.

recommendation.title: Collect proof before auth changes
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted Gateway logs, the failed `connect` frame details, exact CLI/Gateway/package versions, and before/after generated config before changing code or packaging.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across Gateway protocol compatibility, client package extraction, and protocol docs for this boundary.
